equivalents.note: The verse reads rang gnas, 'its own place' or 'abiding in itself', where the Bengali has apaiṭhāna, 'non-abiding'; Munidatta's Tibetan comment has the standard rab tu mi gnas pa (cp.34.m4).
The Tibetan gives the three cries as rgyal po rgyal po nyid kyi rgyal (roughly 'king, the king of kingship itself') and abara rāa as gzhan yang rgyal po, 'another king' or 'and again the king'.
The verse has sa bcu, 'ten stages', against the Bengali's twelve (dvādaśa) and against Munidatta's Tibetan comment, which has sa bcu gnyis pa (cp.34.m6).
For re vaṭa bālayogin the Tibetan has kye'i byis pa rmongs pa'i rnal 'byor pa, so vaṭa comes out as rmongs pa, 'deluded, foolish', taking the address as scornful.

The Tibetan renders pakṣyāpakṣya as phyogs dang phyogs min, 'sides and non-sides', but the following pakṣaṃ na paśyāmy aham as 'I see nothing at all' (bdag gis cung zad kyang ni ma mthong), without phyogs.

The Tibetan construes the number with the Jina, sa bcu gnyis pa'i rgyal ba dang mtshungs pa, 'equal to the Jina of the twelfth stage', where the Sanskrit has 'we who have the twelve stages are equal to the Jinas'.

questions: gagana at cp.34.1b: the Tibetan of 1b has no word for the sky (rnam par rol pa dA ri ka / pha rol mchog gi 'gram du song). The Tibetan words the two halves of the refrain differently, and nam mkha' stands only in 2b, where it is already matched.

lila at cp.34.2b: the Tibetan of 2b has no counterpart of bilasai (dA ri ka pa nam mkha' la / pha rol mchog gi 'gram du song). rnam par rol pa stands in 1b (already matched), and 2a has bde ba chen pos rnam par rol, 'plays by great bliss'.

lila at cp.34.m4: for Munidatta's apratiṣṭhānamahāsukhalīlayā the Tibetan has rab tu mi gnas pa'i bde ba chen por thim pa'i phyir, 'because of dissolving into non-abiding great bliss'. thim pa renders līna, 'absorbed' (the verse's līṇe, where the Tibetan line 3b also has thim), not līlā, so there is no word for play to give.
